```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# The worked example needs monocle3 and BPCells (neither is on CRAN). Where they
# are missing the code is shown but not run.
have_stack <- all(vapply(
  c("projectData", "monocle3", "BPCells", "SingleCellExperiment",
    "SummarizedExperiment", "Matrix"),
  requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE
))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = have_stack)
```

This vignette is for **dataset authors**: people who want to ship a Monocle 3
`cell_data_set` (CDS) whose counts live in a
[BPCells](https://github.com/bnprks/BPCells) on-disk matrix as part of an
ordinary R package. People who only *use* such a package should read
`vignette("using-monocle3-data", package = "projectData.monocle3")`. How the
files are stored, restored and kept alive is explained in
`vignette("storage", package = "projectData.monocle3")`.

## The problem, and who does what

A CDS whose counts are a BPCells matrix holds only a *reference* to a directory
on the author's disk, so `save()` and `saveRDS()` give a file that is useless on
another machine. Monocle's own `save_monocle_objects()` and
`load_monocle_objects()` handle this by copying the matrix directory, but a
data package needs help at both ends: something has to save the directory into
the package, and something has to restore it, at first access, from a read-only
installation. If the object is comfortable in memory, ship it as an ordinary
`.rda` dataset instead; no adapter is needed.

| `projectData` (core) | `projectData.monocle3` (this adapter) |
|---|---|
| Registers installed data packages, builds the catalog from metadata | Declares the loader `projectData.monocle3::cds` |
| Resolves names, attaches collections, handles conflicts | Saves a CDS into a package source tree, writes the placeholder and manifest entry |
| Opens a resource lazily on first access, caches and retries it | Restores the CDS with Monocle's own loader |
| Allocates a private working directory for each opening | Puts the restored BPCells files in that directory |

`projectData` is described in `vignette("projectData", package = "projectData")`
and the adapter mechanism in `vignette("adapters", package = "projectData")`.
The same division of work is used by `projectData.Seurat` for Seurat v5 objects;
the two adapters have similar entry points but different persistence mechanisms
(see `vignette("storage", package = "projectData.monocle3")`).

## Prerequisites

Authoring needs `monocle3`, `BPCells`, `SingleCellExperiment` and
`SummarizedExperiment` in addition to `projectData` and this package. BPCells
and monocle3 are not on CRAN; with `pak`, which also resolves monocle3's
Bioconductor dependencies for your version of R:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak(c(
  "projectData",
  "bnprks/BPCells/r",
  "cole-trapnell-lab/monocle3",
  "blaserlab/projectData.monocle3"
))
```

```{r libs, message = FALSE}
library(monocle3)
library(projectData.monocle3)
work <- file.path(tempdir(), "authoring-demo")
dir.create(work)
```

## 1. Create a small CDS

A synthetic CDS with sparse integer counts, cell and gene metadata, an extra
in-memory assay and a UMAP embedding. In practice this is your real object.

```{r cds}
set.seed(9215)
genes <- sprintf("gene%02d", 1:40)
cells <- sprintf("cell%02d", 1:25)
counts <- matrix(rpois(40 * 25, 2), 40, 25, dimnames = list(genes, cells))
# Every gene and cell must be observed
counts[cbind(1:40, (1:40 %% 25) + 1)] <- 3
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(counts, sparse = TRUE)

cds <- new_cell_data_set(
  counts,
  cell_metadata = data.frame(row.names = cells, group = rep(c("a", "b"), length.out = 25)),
  gene_metadata = data.frame(row.names = genes, gene_short_name = toupper(genes))
)
SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "logcounts") <- log1p(as.matrix(counts))
SingleCellExperiment::reducedDims(cds) <- list(UMAP = cbind(cos(1:25), sin(1:25)))

class(SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "counts"))
```

The counts are an ordinary in-memory `dgCMatrix`. They do not have to be
BPCells-backed already: see step 4.

## 2. Prepare an ordinary R package

A data package is an R package whose source directory has a `DESCRIPTION`
(create it as you would any other, for example with `usethis::create_package()`).
The adapter requires only that the directory has a `DESCRIPTION` with a
`Package` field, because `save_monocle_cds()` refuses to write anywhere else.

```{r skeleton}
pkg <- file.path(work, "myMonocleData")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: myMonocleData",
  "Title: Example Monocle 3 Data",
  "Version: 0.1.0",
  "Authors@R: person('Ada', 'Author', email = 'ada@example.com', role = c('aut', 'cre'))",
  "Description: A tiny synthetic data package that ships a disk-backed Monocle 3 CDS.",
  "License: MIT + file LICENSE",
  "Suggests: projectData.monocle3",
  "Encoding: UTF-8"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
writeLines(c("YEAR: 2026", "COPYRIGHT HOLDER: Ada Author"), file.path(pkg, "LICENSE"))
writeLines(character(), file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"))
```

`projectData.monocle3` is listed in `Suggests`: your users need it only to open
the object, and projectData loads it (without attaching it) from the manifest.
If you distribute the package from a repository that does not carry
`projectData.monocle3`, add it to `Remotes` as well.

## 3. Save the CDS into the package

```{r save}
res <- save_monocle_cds(cds, name = "demo_cds", package_dir = pkg)
```

`name` must be a syntactically valid R name; it becomes the saved directory, the
placeholder, the manifest resource and the object users will access. The call
returns, invisibly, a list describing what happened:

```{r result}
str(res[c("name", "manifest_status", "replaced", "removed_stale")])
```

The call does not modify `cds`, does not edit `R/data.R`, and writes nothing to
the working directory. It validates everything first (the name, the counts, any
existing files and the manifest), then builds the files in a hidden staging
directory inside the package, checks them with the loader's own validation and
only then moves them into place. If anything fails the previous state is
restored. It is not a filesystem transaction: if R is killed mid-commit, a
hidden `.projectData.monocle3-stage-*` directory may remain and may hold the
previous files.

## 4. Counts are converted to BPCells automatically

The package is meant for CDS objects whose counts are a BPCells directory. What
`save_monocle_cds()` does depends on what it finds:

| `counts` in the CDS | Handling |
|---|---|
| BPCells directory matrix (`MatrixDir`), including lazy subsets | Saved as it is, without reconversion |
| `dgCMatrix` / `dgTMatrix`, or a BPCells in-memory matrix | Converted automatically with Monocle, on a **copy** of the CDS |
| Dense `matrix`, `DelayedMatrix`, HDF5-backed BPCells, `lgCMatrix`, no `counts` | **Error**, before anything is written |

Here the counts were a `dgCMatrix`, so a BPCells directory was written into the
package, while `cds` is unchanged:

```{r converted}
class(SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "counts"))
list.files(file.path(pkg, "inst", "extdata", "demo_cds", "bpcells_matrix_dir"))
```

Conversion applies to `counts` only. Other assays are never converted (see
"What is refused" below).

## 5. The generated package layout

```{r layout}
list.files(pkg, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE)
```

* `inst/extdata/demo_cds/` is a directory written by Monocle's native
  `save_monocle_objects()` with no tar archive, so the BPCells matrix and
  Monocle's index files are installed as ordinary files.
* `data/demo_cds.rda` is the **placeholder**.
* `inst/projectData/manifest.dcf` is the manifest entry.

### The placeholder is not the CDS

The placeholder is mandatory, not configurable. It exists so that `data()`,
`R CMD check` and roxygen2 treat the dataset conventionally. It is a small
classed character vector that prints its own instructions with base R, without
projectData or this package:

```{r placeholder}
load(file.path(pkg, "data", "demo_cds.rda"))
demo_cds
rm(demo_cds)
```

`data("demo_cds")` therefore gives only this text, and, if you load it into the
global environment, it can mask the real object attached by projectData. Remove
it with `rm(demo_cds)` and use `projectData::data_attach()` or
`projectData::data_get()`.

## 6. The manifest

```{r manifest}
writeLines(readLines(file.path(pkg, "inst", "projectData", "manifest.dcf")))
```

`Source` uses the **installed** layout (`extdata/demo_cds`, not
`inst/extdata/demo_cds`). Each resource declares exactly one object. The manifest
takes precedence over the placeholder for the same name, so projectData resolves
the resource through the loader and never offers the placeholder as the dataset.
(`AdapterExport: projectData_loaders` is the default and is omitted.)

`save_monocle_cds()` registers the resource itself. `write_monocle_manifest()` is
for reconciling the manifest with what is on disk, for example after you saved a
directory by other means or deleted one. It returns, invisibly, a data frame with
one row per resource (`added`, `updated`, `unchanged`, `removed`, `skipped` or
`conflict`). It is idempotent: the file is not rewritten, and no summary is
printed, when nothing changes.

```{r reconcile}
status <- write_monocle_manifest(pkg)
status
```

Reconciliation covers only entries owned by this adapter (loader
`projectData.monocle3::cds`). A saved directory with a valid placeholder is
added or updated, and an entry whose directory or placeholder you deleted is
removed as stale. Entries of other loaders are preserved unchanged; a resource
or object name that another adapter owns is a conflict, reported and left alone.
A manifest that cannot be parsed is never overwritten. Reconciliation never
deletes a saved directory or a placeholder.

## 7. Document the dataset

`save_monocle_cds()` never edits `R/data.R` and tells you when it finds no
`"demo_cds"` documentation line. Document the dataset as you would any other:

```{r document}
writeLines(c(
  "#' Demonstration Monocle 3 dataset",
  "#'",
  "#' @format A Monocle 3 `cell_data_set` with BPCells-backed counts.",
  "#' @details Access with `projectData::data_attach()`.",
  "#' @source Synthetic.",
  "\"demo_cds\""
), file.path(pkg, "R", "data.R"))
```

In a real package run `devtools::document()` to generate `man/demo_cds.Rd`. To
keep this example free of roxygen2, write the equivalent Rd file directly:

```{r rd}
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "man"))
writeLines(c(
  "\\name{demo_cds}", "\\alias{demo_cds}", "\\docType{data}",
  "\\title{Demonstration Monocle 3 dataset}",
  "\\format{A Monocle 3 cell_data_set with BPCells-backed counts.}",
  "\\description{Access it with \\code{projectData::data_attach()}.}",
  "\\keyword{datasets}"
), file.path(pkg, "man", "demo_cds.Rd"))
```

Practical notes for the real package:

* The placeholder `data/<name>.rda` must be **part of the package source**. If
  your `.gitignore` excludes `*.rda`, add `!data/<name>.rda`, or the placeholder
  (and with it the manifest entry) will be missing from fresh checkouts.
* Keep the script that generates the CDS in `inst/data-raw/`.
* The BPCells files count towards the size of the package. Check the size limits
  of wherever you distribute it; CRAN, for example, expects far smaller packages
  than a typical single-cell dataset.

## 8. Build and install the data package

Installation is ordinary. Here it goes into a temporary library:

```{r install-pkg}
lib <- file.path(work, "library")
dir.create(lib)
install.packages(pkg, lib = lib, repos = NULL, type = "source", quiet = TRUE)
list.files(file.path(lib, "myMonocleData", "extdata", "demo_cds"))
```

The installed resource is read-only data: nothing below writes to it.

## 9. Load it through projectData

```{r load}
library(projectData)
data_config(messages = FALSE)
restored <- data_get("demo_cds", package = "myMonocleData", lib.loc = lib)
class(restored)
dim(restored)
```

`data_get()` registered the package and opened the resource on this first
access. `data_attach("myMonocleData")` would register it and let you use the bare
name `demo_cds`; see `vignette("using-monocle3-data", package = "projectData.monocle3")`.

## 10. Verify the result

The restored object has the same counts, metadata, extra assay and reduction as
the original, which can be checked here because the object is small:

```{r verify}
all.equal(as(SummarizedExperiment::assay(restored, "counts"), "dgCMatrix"), counts)
identical(as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(restored))[, "group", drop = FALSE],
          as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(cds))[, "group", drop = FALSE])
all.equal(SummarizedExperiment::assay(restored, "logcounts"),
          SummarizedExperiment::assay(cds, "logcounts"))
all.equal(SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(restored, "UMAP"),
          SingleCellExperiment::reducedDim(cds, "UMAP"))
```

The counts are still a BPCells matrix, and the files they read were restored
into the working directory that projectData allocated for this opening, not into
the installed package or the original author's directory:

```{r backing}
count_dir <- BPCells::all_matrix_inputs(SummarizedExperiment::assay(restored, "counts"))[[1]]@dir
class(SummarizedExperiment::assay(restored, "counts"))
startsWith(normalizePath(count_dir), normalizePath(file.path(tempdir(), "projectData-work")))
```

The restored CDS keeps working after the collection is detached (detaching
forgets the collection; it never deletes backing files):

```{r detach}
data_detach()
sum(colSums(SummarizedExperiment::assay(restored, "counts")))
```

## Replacing a dataset

Saving a name that already exists needs `overwrite = TRUE`, and only replaces
what this package can show that it wrote. An existing directory is replaceable
when at least two of three kinds of evidence agree: a native Monocle file
index, a manifest entry of this loader, and a recognized placeholder, and nothing
else is in the directory. A directory that merely looks like a Monocle save, a
directory that another loader's manifest entry claims, and a `data/<name>.rda`
that holds anything but a placeholder are never replaced.

```{r overwrite, error = TRUE}
save_monocle_cds(cds, name = "demo_cds", package_dir = pkg)
```

```{r overwrite-ok}
invisible(save_monocle_cds(cds, name = "demo_cds", package_dir = pkg, overwrite = TRUE))
```

## What is refused

Everything that cannot be shipped faithfully is refused **before anything is
written**. The most common case is a secondary assay that is itself stored on
disk. Monocle would save it only as a reference to its original directory, which
does not exist for your users:

```{r refused, error = TRUE}
adt <- matrix(rpois(3 * 25, 5), 3, 25, dimnames = list(paste0("adt", 1:3), cells))
adt <- suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(BPCells::write_matrix_dir(
  BPCells::convert_matrix_type(as(Matrix::Matrix(adt, sparse = TRUE), "IterableMatrix"), "double"),
  file.path(work, "adt")
)))
external <- cds
SingleCellExperiment::altExp(external, "ADT") <- SingleCellExperiment::SingleCellExperiment(
  assays = list(counts = adt)
)
save_monocle_cds(external, name = "other_cds", package_dir = pkg)
```

The error has class `projectData.monocle3_external_assay` and names every
offender, at any nesting depth. Convert such assays to in-memory matrices or drop
them; the adapter never does it for you because it could need a lot of memory.
The complete list of supported and refused representations is in
`vignette("storage", package = "projectData.monocle3")`.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
try(data_detach(), silent = TRUE)
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
